In other cases, -ed is just a consonant attached to the end: /t/ after voiceless sounds, /d/ after voiced sounds and vowels.
Người Việt thường bỏ hẳn -ed (“I work th: Vietnamese people often omit the -ed (“I work there last year”), or read every -ed as /ɪd/ (“work-ed”, “stop-ed”) making the word have an extra syllable. Another mistake is reading by word: “increased” ends with the letter “e” but the final sound of “increase” is voiceless /s/ so -ed reads /t/. Correction: determine the final sound of the base verb, then connect -ed to the next word (“developed_a plan” → /dɪˈveləptə/).
